full_body:
Asian equity markets started the week on a positive note as easing oil prices and hopes of a steady US interest rate outlook lifted investor sentiment. Wall Street futures also traded higher ahead of the upcoming earnings season in the United States. South Korea's benchmark index continued its strong run, supported by optimism around artificial intelligence-related chip demand, while Nikkei traded marginally lower.

Around 8:40 am IST, Japan's Nikkei was trading 1.18% lower, while South Korea's Kospi tumbled 3%. In contrast, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index (HSI) bucked the trend, rising 0.78%.

Investors globally are increasingly shifting their attention from monetary policy concerns towards corporate earnings, particularly expectations of strong profits from technology companies benefiting from the AI boom. Positive global cues could provide additional support to the Dalal Street at the opening bell.

Among India's most valuable listed companies, Bharti Airtel and Bajaj Finance emerged as the biggest wealth creators during the previous week. Bharti Airtel added over Rs 36,500 crore to its market capitalisation, taking its valuation above Rs 11.63 lakh crore. Bajaj Finance followed closely with an increase of more than Rs 33,000 crore.

ICICI Bank, LIC, HDFC Bank and Hindustan Unilever also posted gains in market value. The surge reflects continued investor confidence in sectors ranging from telecom and financial services to consumer goods, even as broader market sentiment remained supported by improving domestic fundamentals and favourable global developments.

Apart from domestic earnings, investors across global markets are awaiting fresh signals from the US Federal Reserve. Following softer-than-expected US labour market data, expectations have grown that the central bank may avoid another interest rate hike in the near term. Futures currently indicate a strong possibility that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its July meeting.

Attention now turns to the minutes of the Fed's June policy meeting, scheduled later this week, which could offer insights into policymakers' assessment of inflation and economic growth. Any indication of a less aggressive monetary stance would likely support equities worldwide, including markets such as India.

Oil prices are likely to remain one of the biggest drivers for Indian equities this week as global crude continues to trade at relatively comfortable levels. Brent crude has slipped near four-month lows while US crude also eased after OPEC+ agreed to further raise production targets from August. Concerns over supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz have also moderated, easing pressure on global energy markets.

headline: Why are there concerns over WhatsApp usernames? | Explained
body: What is the username feature that WhatsApp intends to roll out? How does it work and what privacy safeguards are built into it? Why is the Indian government asking WhatsApp to stop its roll-out? Can the government dictate an app’s features?
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

O n July 1, 2026, the Union government sent a notice to Meta asking it to stop the rollout of WhatsApp’s username feature, for which the Meta-owned messaging platform is currently taking reservations. In a notice to the social media platform, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) wrote that hiding phone numbers and only showing usernames may increase the incidence of online fraud, phishing, digital arrest scams and impersonation attacks.

WhatsApp advertises usernames as a way to chat without sharing phone numbers. Instead of a mobile number, new contacts will only see your chosen username. This is an optional feature.

There is no search directory of usernames within WhatsApp. To contact someone, you need to know the person’s exact username. For those who are concerned that someone could guess their username, WhatsApp has said they would be able to set a personal identification number (PIN). In that case, even someone who knows your username will not be able to contact you if they don’t know your PIN.

The feature is yet to be rolled out. Meta has said it will be made widely available over the next few months with multiple safeguards in place.

MeitY said in its notice, a copy of which was reviewed by The Hindu, that the feature could “facilitate impersonation and identity spoofing, including impersonation of individuals, public authorities, financial institutions, and government agencies, by permitting the adoption of usernames closely resembling those of genuine persons or institutions”.

Echoing MeitY’s concerns, some public personalities have said that variations of their names have already been reserved by users. In a post on X, MobiKwik founder Bipin Preet Singh said this had happened to him. He wrote: “Not a good idea at all. Will lead to proliferation of fraud and impersonation.”

The EU's top court will decide Thursday whether to uphold a record 4.1 billion euro ($4.7 billion) fine the bloc slapped on Google for anti-competitive practices related to its Android operating system.

It is the second attempt by the U.S. tech giant to overturn the penalty imposed by the European Commission in 2018, which remains the bloc's highest ever antitrust fine.

The commission, the EU's antitrust regulator, had accused Google of abusing the popularity of its Android operating system to restrict competition.

It alleged Google pressured phone makers using Android to pre-install its search engine and Google Chrome browser, essentially shutting out rivals, and ordered it to pay a 4.3-billion-euro fine.

The findings were upheld in 2022 by the General Court, the EU's second-highest. But the Luxembourg-based body slightly reduced the levy to 4.1 billion euros, still the EU's biggest ever.

Google filed a new challenge arguing before the bloc's top court, the European Court of Justice, that the case was unfounded and that the sanction penalised innovation.
